newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says gap with Israel bigger than thought.
newsitem.headline: PLO says gap with Israel bigger than thought.

text.p: The gap in Israeli-Palestinian peacemaking is far bigger than people think, PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat said on Sunday.
"So far the Israeli government still insists on continuing settlement activities and I think the gap between the two sides is much bigger than people think," he told Israel Radio.
Talks have been in crisis since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu broke ground in March on a Jewish settlement on the outskirts of Arab East Jerusalem.

"As long as Mr Netanyahu continues his settlement activities and confiscation of land and building in Abu Ghneim and other areas, I don't think we will have a meaningful negotiation or a meaningful peace process," Erekat said.
Several hours after Erekat spoke to the radio, Netanyahu met Egyptian envoy Osama al-Baz. Netanyahu's office said in a statement afterward:

"There was some progress in the meeting towards solving the problems between Israel and the Palestinian Authority. Al-Baz's contacts with the sides are to continue. No additional meeting has been set with al-Baz who returns today to Cairo."

Erekat had been set to meet al-Baz as well but told Reuters al-Baz had to return to Cairo after meeting Netanyahu. Erekat said on Monday Egyptian Ambassador to Israel Mohammed Bassiouny would brief him on al-Baz's meeting with Netanyahu.
A PLO official who spoke on condition he not be named said: "Al-Baz did not get responses from the Israeli side to Palestinian demands" to stop settlement.

An Egyptian government newspaper had said al-Baz would seek "to find out Netanyahu's reaction to Palestinian proposals" emerging from a meeting al-Baz had with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat a few days ago.
"Mr Netanyahu must stop, must freeze settlement activities, if he wants to give a chance to the peace process, if he wants to have a negotiation that has a meaning," Erekat told the radio.
